claims.claim_text: The European Commission reported in October 2026 that connected photovoltaic installations create cyber-risk scenarios relevant to EU electricity-system resilience.
claims.contrary_evidence: No contrary evidence reviewed for the stated publication finding.
claims.sector_relevance: Distributed generation expands reliance on inverter, installer, maintenance and control ecosystems.
claims.limitations: The report is guidance and does not establish an incident or implementation rate.

claims.claim_text: ENISA's September 2026 threat publication identifies cyber dependencies and third-party integration as routes through which one compromise can have broader effects.
claims.contrary_evidence: The source is cross-sector and does not measure energy-provider concentration.
claims.sector_relevance: Shared digital dependencies can create correlated disruption pathways for digitally connected energy operators.
claims.limitations: The publication is based on cross-sector observations and does not constitute September energy incident telemetry.

claims.claim_text: The December 2025 Polish incident caused loss of communication and prevented remote control at at least 30 wind and solar farms, while generation continued and power-system stability was not affected.
claims.contrary_evidence: The report records no generation interruption or power-system-stability effect.
claims.sector_relevance: Loss of observability and dispatch control can require operating restrictions even when supply continues.
claims.limitations: The source does not disclose financial loss, recovery cost or customer compensation.

claims.claim_text: A July 2026 joint advisory records Iranian-affiliated actors accessing internet-reachable PLCs, changing control logic and HMI or SCADA displays, and disabling some shutdown and alarm logic at affected organisations including energy-sector entities.
claims.exact_locator: S-003 sections Ongoing Threat Actor Activity, Initial Access, Exfiltration and Impact
claims.contrary_evidence: No EU or UK energy victim is named in the advisory.
claims.sector_relevance: Externally reachable engineering and remote-access paths can affect control integrity and operator visibility.
claims.limitations: US-focused evidence used as a threat-pattern proxy, not EU or UK victim evidence.

claims.claim_text: A 2026 joint ransomware advisory describes exploitation of internet-facing VPN and firewall appliances and lists utilities among victim sectors in Europe.
claims.exact_locator: S-004 opening section and Technical Details sections Overview and Initial Access
claims.contrary_evidence: The advisory does not identify a named European utility or September 2026 event.
claims.sector_relevance: Internet-facing remote access and perimeter appliances can be common access dependencies in utilities.
claims.limitations: Leak-site observations are not a complete victim census.

claims.claim_text: Energy cyber impact can transmit from a digital intrusion through loss of visibility or operating restrictions into recovery demand, service disruption, market effects and counterparty pressure.
claims.exact_locator: S-003 Impact; S-005 pp. 4-12; S-010 Federal Agency Actions; S-011 sections II-IV; S-012 Action Update
alternative_hypotheses: Some intrusions remain contained within enterprise environments and do not affect energy operations.
Operational restrictions may prevent downstream service disruption where manual fallback and segmentation are effective.
claims.contrary_evidence: S-005 records continued generation and no power-system-stability effect despite loss of remote control.
claims.sector_relevance: The judgment frames sector transmission mechanisms without estimating any bank or operator loss.
claims.limitations: No selected source provides a comparable EU or UK September 2026 loss or outage data series.

claims.claim_text: Scenario A assumes disruption of a shared ICT, communications, control or managed-service dependency used by multiple energy entities, causing correlated degradation of visibility, command, scheduling or support functions.
claims.exact_locator: S-002 pp. 12, 43 and 96; S-009 Article 18 and Article 19
alternative_hypotheses: Dependency failures remain limited to one operator where architectures are diversified.
A service outage is resolved before any energy-service effect occurs.
claims.contrary_evidence: No selected source identifies a named common provider or quantifies concentration across European utilities.
claims.sector_relevance: Tests correlated dependency exposure across digitalised energy operations.
claims.limitations: No provider name, probability, outage duration or loss figure is assumed.

claims.claim_text: Scenario B assumes access to an exposed engineering, perimeter or remote-access component supporting distributed generation, followed by altered logic or loss of operator visibility and conservative operating restrictions.
claims.exact_locator: S-003 Initial Access and Impact; S-005 pp. 4-12
alternative_hypotheses: The access attempt is blocked before control-system impact.
Remote-control loss occurs without supply interruption or sector effect.
claims.contrary_evidence: S-005 documents continued generation and no system-stability effect in the Polish case.
claims.sector_relevance: Tests whether loss of control and visibility can create operational constraints before supply stops.
claims.limitations: The scenario is not a claim of a current European campaign or a forecast.

claims.claim_text: Scenario C assumes ransomware or destructive activity affects enterprise and support networks, uncertainty over operational-technology separation prompts operating restrictions, and disruption transmits through energy customers, fuel, transport, market or public-service dependencies.
claims.exact_locator: S-005 pp. 4-12; S-010 opening and Federal Agency Actions; S-011 sections II-IV; S-012 Action Update
alternative_hypotheses: Network segmentation and manual fallback confine the event.
Public-authority measures reduce secondary supply effects before they widen.
claims.contrary_evidence: No selected source establishes an equivalent September 2026 EU or UK cascade.
claims.sector_relevance: Tests the linkage from enterprise intrusion to sector-wide operating and supply dependencies.
claims.limitations: The historical Colonial case is US context and is not an EU or UK loss benchmark.

claims.claim_text: On 7 May 2021, Colonial Pipeline stopped its system after identifying ransomware in order to contain the intrusion and protect operational technology; the company began returning pipelines to service on 12 May and DOE records restart on 13 May.
claims.exact_locator: S-010 opening and status updates; S-011 sections II and IV
claims.contrary_evidence: The sources use different restart-milestone descriptions but both establish restoration beginning after the shutdown period.
claims.sector_relevance: Historical illustration of precautionary shutdown and restoration coordination when IT-to-OT separation cannot be established.
claims.limitations: US oil-products pipeline context, not evidence of an EU or UK utility event or requirement.

claims.claim_text: The EU electricity network code requires risk-assessment methods to consider dependency on a single ICT product, service or process supplier, cascading effects and Union-wide consequences for cross-border electricity flows.
claims.contrary_evidence: The regulation requires assessment methods but does not state that any named supplier is concentrated.
claims.sector_relevance: Formal electricity-sector basis for monitoring dependency and cross-border propagation pathways.
claims.limitations: The regulation is enduring context and does not establish a September 2026 event or bank obligation.

claims.claim_text: The United Kingdom's August 2026 downstream gas and electricity consultation proposes reviewing the NIS perimeter and a baseline cyber-resilience requirement for Ofgem licensees, subject to legislation and further consultation.
claims.exact_locator: S-007 Regulatory environment and Section 1 Proposed approach
claims.contrary_evidence: The source expressly states that changes are subject to later legislative and consultation steps.
claims.sector_relevance: Public regulatory monitoring item for Great Britain energy-sector perimeter and baseline requirements.
claims.limitations: Proposal only; does not apply across the EU or establish completed implementation.

claims.claim_text: Public EU guidance identifies controlled inverter communications, firmware-update controls, qualified installers and protection of installer maintenance systems as relevant mitigation themes for connected photovoltaic assets.
claims.contrary_evidence: The guidance does not establish implementation rates or outcome effectiveness.
claims.sector_relevance: Creates publicly observable comparator themes for connected generation and maintenance ecosystems.
claims.limitations: Guidance is not evidence of a utility's control effectiveness or a legal requirement.
